rationale: Round 3, lens: AC falsifiability and internal consistency, re-read from disk at 4c46cf64. All 7 of my round-2 asks are ADDRESSED (blocking-vs-informational near-misses with AC-4 (v)/(vi); the nothing-failing scoped-flag rule with an AC-15 leg; R1.4 keyed on the tally with AC-4 (iii-a)/(iii-b); AC-11 (iii)/(iii-neg) topology; the undirected-form residual and the no-panel-only confirmation rule; R1.8 (c) dispatch into T; the AC-16 determinism leg). I accept the refutation of my round-2 BRIEF item: the only 'TODO(skill)' string in the BRIEF today is the sentence refuting me. One MAJOR remains, found by attacking the new selection rule with a scratch bd 1.1.0 database: bd mints the plan-form ID for ANY child created under an epic (`bd create --type bug --parent E` -> `<E>.2`, `--type feature` -> `<E>.3`, both returned by bd ready with parent E). Under R1.1 (type is not a membership input; lineage by parent edge) such a follow-up bug is a MEMBER, not the 'informational near-miss' that R1.2, OQ-7 and AC-4 (v) describe. In a review-phase spec with one open follow-up bug under E, the member set is {bug}: R1.4's derived-state block is never printed, the default pick selects the bug, MF-1 fails (no `## Bead N` for it), and every scoped `next` exits non-zero — the exact permanent failure OQ-7 says it prevents. The spec's informational class and AC-4 (v) are reachable only for a bug reparented after creation, which no shipped flow does. Three minors: AC-1's bead G is red-on-revert only under an unpinned fake-bd `--parent` semantics; GateReadiness's behaviour for a scoped override whose named signal carries an `indeterminate` record is unstated (the reader will never cover it); AC-11 (vii) does not say whether `reattest` WRITES in O3's shape. Everything else I re-derived holds; see the verified list.
concrete_changes_required: R1.1/R1.2/OQ-7/AC-4 (v): state that a non-lifecycle bead minted under E (bd gives it `<E>.<N>` and `parent: E`, verified on bd 1.1.0 for `bug` and `feature`) IS a member, and that R1.2's 'non-lifecycle children' informational class covers only a non-plan-form (reparented) child. Then decide and pin the common shape: recommend that the DEFAULT pick (no positional, `--pick` 0) selects the first LIFECYCLE member, that non-lifecycle members stay listed and claimable by positional or `--pick`, and that when every member is non-lifecycle the R1.4 derived-state block is printed as well. Add an AC-1 row 'B: `<E>.5`, parent E, type bug' with its expected classification (member, not default-picked) and rewrite AC-4 (v) so the follow-up bug is explicitly the reparented non-plan-form shape, or move it to the new default-pick fixture.

AC-1 (bead G red-on-revert): on bd 1.1.0 `bd ready --parent E` returns a detached `<E>.<N>` row by ID prefix and G's full-spec-ID title passes today's `containsSpecID`, so G is selectable at 7a490064 and the leg is red only if the fake bd is edge-only. Pin one of: the fake bd's `--parent` is edge-only (the reporter's apparent bd), or G's title carries only the numeric tag `[<NNN>] …` (which `FindEpicForBead`'s `fmt.Sscanf("%d")` fallback still resolves and today's full-ID filter drops).

R6.1/R6.2: state what `GateReadiness` does when a NAMED signal's current failure set contains an `indeterminate` record (a membership or landed-merge read error). R6.2 says such a record is never coverable on the reader side; if the writer still proceeds and records it, the claim succeeds and `ready-check` then refuses dispatch — two answers for one state. Recommend: refuse the scoped override before any mutation with 'MF-3 carries an infrastructure failure that no override covers' and add the leg to AC-15.

AC-11 (vii): state whether `ReattestLandedMerge` WRITES a binding for the nominated short-form merge (second parent A) in that fixture, given that X's later reviewed tip B never landed and only the operator warning is emitted. 'nominates the merge and renders the caveat and warning' leaves the write outcome, which is the fixture's whole point, unpinned.

findings.title: Round-2 ask status
findings.detail: F2r2.1 (near-miss exit policy) ADDRESSED — R1.2 defines blocking (N1, N2, lifecycle-type N3 under E) vs informational (title-only, metadata-only, non-lifecycle children); R1.4 exit codes and OQ-7 follow; AC-4 (v) exits 0 with a bug child and a title hit, (vi) exits non-zero with a detached plan-form bead. (See the MAJOR below for the shape this class does not reach.) F2r2.2 (R6.1 nothing-failing) ADDRESSED — R6.1 bullet 2: normal claim, note printed, no marker, no --evidence; AC-15 last leg. F2r2.3 (keyed on tally; AC-4 iii) ADDRESSED — R1.4 item 4 'keyed on the tally' with the two-tallies-to-plan rationale; AC-4 (iii-a) implement / (iii-b) plan pinned. F2r2.4 (AC-11 iii) ADDRESSED — (iii) states X's own `Merge bead/X` landing and that the long-form X->Y merge is excluded; (iii-neg) pins NoCandidate when Y is the only path. F2r2.5 (undirected form overclaim) ADDRESSED — R4.2 'No target guarantee for the undirected form', the (b)/(d)-only confirmation rule on the fallback path, and the stated residual; ADR-0041 amendment item (i) is listed in AC-18 with the same content. F2r2.6 (R1.8 no-resolved-spec) ADDRESSED — R1.8 (c): the dispatch spec is T, never HEAD; AC-6 (c) pins the branch base. F2r2.7 (digest determinism) ADDRESSED — AC-16 'Determinism' leg plus writer/reader agreement over a control byte. Totals: 7 ADDRESSED, 0 PARTIAL, 0 MISSED; 1 NEW_ISSUE raised below from attacking the new selection rule.

findings.title: A follow-up bug created under the epic is a plan-form MEMBER, so R1.2's informational class, OQ-7's rationale and AC-4 (v) describe a shape the normal flow never produces
findings.detail: Verified in a scratch bd 1.1.0 database: `bd create --type bug --parent <E>` -> `<E>.2` (issue_type bug), `--type feature` -> `<E>.3`; `bd ready --json -n 0` returns both with `parent: <E>`. R1.1: 'issue_type is not a membership input' and lineage holds by the parent edge, so these rows are MEMBERS. R1.2/OQ-7/AC-4 (v) treat 'a follow-up bug under E' as an informational near-miss; AC-1's F is explicitly 'non-plan-form, parent E, type bug', a shape only `bd update --parent` on a bead created elsewhere produces. Consequence for the common shape: in a review-phase spec with one open follow-up bug under E the member set is {bug}, R1.4's derived-state block is not printed (the set is non-empty), the default pick (SelectWork pick==0 -> items[0]) selects the bug, MF-1 fails for lack of a `## Bead N` section, and every scoped `next` exits non-zero — OQ-7's 'one permanently ready follow-up bead ... would fail every scoped next forever', now via membership instead of the exit code. The repo's own code anticipates bugs being claimed through next (cmd/mindspec/next.go advancePhaseOnClaim guards on phase.IsLifecycleIssueType). The spec needs to say which it wants and pin it.

findings.title: AC-1's bead G is red-on-revert only under an unpinned fake-bd `--parent` semantics
findings.detail: The AC itself hedges: 'today G is excluded on an edge-only --parent bd, or when its title lacks the full spec ID'. G's title is `[S] …` with the full spec ID, which today's containsSpecID keeps, and bd 1.1.0's `--parent` returns a detached `<E>.<N>` by prefix (Background A), so on a bd-1.1.0-faithful fake G is selectable at 7a490064. phase.FindEpicForBead's fallback parses the title tag with fmt.Sscanf("%d"), so a numeric-only `[129] …` tag resolves lineage while failing today's full-ID filter; pin that, or pin the fake's `--parent` as edge-only.

findings.title: Scoped override over an `indeterminate` record: writer and reader disagree
findings.detail: R6.2: 'An MF-3 record of class indeterminate ... is never coverable'. R6.1: GateReadiness 'proceeds iff the currently failing set is a SUBSET of the named set' — an MF-3 that fails with an indeterminate record is in the failing set and MF-3 can be named, so the claim proceeds and a fingerprint over the indeterminate record is written; `ready-check` then reports MF-3 uncovered and the dispatch ingress stops. No AC covers the GateReadiness side.

findings.title: AC-11 (vii) leaves reattest's write outcome unpinned
findings.detail: R4.3 lets reattest proceed 'on its other data (at minimum (a))' and R4.2 says a fallback candidate is 'confirmed ONLY by (b) or (d)' for FindLandedMergeReachable while reattest 'stays the exit'. In (vii) there is no (b) or (d) and X's later tip B never landed; the AC says reattest 'nominates the merge and renders' the caveat and warning but not whether it writes the binding. That is the falsifiable fact the fixture exists to pin.

findings.title: Verified against 4c46cf64 / live tools (no change needed)
findings.detail: Selection rule attack: a plan-form ID `<E>.<N>` is minted only under E, and R1.8 (a)/(b) require PlanBeadIndex(E_T, id) and S == T, so a bead of another spec cannot be selected or dispatched; a detached `<E>.<N>` with a `[130]` tag resolves lineage to E130 and becomes N2 for S and non-plan-form for 130. FindEpicForBead's dependency leg takes the first epic-typed dependency and its title leg parses leading digits (fmt.Sscanf %d), matching the consolidation's `[129-probe]` evidence. Fallback confirmation rule: AC-11 (vii) (panel-only -> NoEvidence), (viii) (tip confirms short form into Y), (ix) (ambiguity resolved only by (b)/(d)) are consistent with R4.2 and with R4.3's decision rule and binding veto; the CLOSE-path reach argument (exact match confirms, non-matching set -> NoEvidence -> MergedUnclosed error, never a close) is sound. Fingerprint: records are raw, sorted, deduplicated, free of text/timestamps; VALID requires one 64-hex entry per signal; AC-16/17 cover A-then-A+B, MF-4 second blocker, determinism, writer/reader agreement, and the malformed list was updated from digest to fingerprint. R2.2/AC-7 tolerate-explicit-`-n 0` and reject-cap legs are consistent with the lint (ListJSON's first bd arg is not the literal). ADR diffs in 4c46cf64 match AC-18 (Decision 5 transition clause, ADR-0044 back-pointer grandfathered until step 7, ADR-0040 back-pointer naming L3's gain). BRIEF grep: the only `TODO(skill)` occurrence is the Round-3 sentence refuting the round-2 claim; the two `<!-- -->` markers are the machine header.

My round-2 'TODO(skill) placeholders remain' claim is correctly refuted — I wrote it from round-1 memory instead of re-reading the file.
